questions.q: About how many fungi have adopted a 'carnivorous' lifestyle?
The carnivorous fungi are drawn from how many phyla?
c: Four fungal phyla and one pseudofungal phylum

questions.q: How many mechanisms for exploiting small animals does Kendrick describe?
Small soil animals are valuable to fungi mainly as a source of protein (nitrogen).

sections.title: Mechanisms for Infecting Nematodes and Other Small Animals

questions.q: *Catenaria* zoospores find nematodes by:
c: Chemotaxis, encysting near the mouth or anus

questions.q: *Haptoglossa* is unique among fungi for producing:
c: 'Harpoon cells' that inject infective material into prey

questions.q: Kendrick compares the *Haptoglossa* harpoon cell to the nematocysts of:
The harpoon cell mechanism is homologous to cnidarian nematocysts.
*Meristacrum* sporangia that miss a nematode:
c: Germinate to form a small adhesive secondary spore on a stalk

*Harposporium anguillulae* conidia infect nematodes by:
c: Being eaten and sticking in the oesophagus

When a nematode tears an adhesive knob loose, what happens?
c: The knob stays stuck to the cuticle and sends in an infective hypha

questions.q: Which trapping device is probably the commonest, recorded in nearly forty species?
The commonest nematode-trapping hyphomycete, with 3D adhesive nets, is:
Why can only eumycotan fungi form adhesive nets?
c: Nets need repeated anastomosis of assimilative hyphae

questions.q: Nonconstricting (detachable) rings catch nematodes by:
c: Fitting snugly and breaking off as a collar around the worm

questions.q: How quickly do the three cells of a constricting ring inflate?
c: In about one-tenth of a second

questions.q: Constricting rings can also be triggered by heat or mechanical stimulation without a nematode.
What allows the ring cells to expand inward so fast?
c: Outer walls rupture along lines of weakness and cells take up water, deploying reserve wall material

questions.q: Why don't many trap-forming fungi make traps all the time?
c: They produce traps only when they detect chemical signs of nematodes

questions.q: Conidia of trap-forming species are usually larger than those of species using sticky or ingested spores because:
c: They carry reserves to build a trap on their own

questions.q: The oyster mushroom, *Pleurotus ostreatus*, secretes a substance that:
Why might nematodes be important to *Pleurotus*?
c: Dead wood, its substrate, is notoriously deficient in nitrogen

questions.q: *Rhopalomyces elegans* parasitizes nematode eggs by:
c: Growing toward them, forming appressoria, and penetrating

questions.q: *Rhopalomyces* can also parasitize adult nematodes.

sections.title: Exploitation of Other Animals and Protists

questions.q: The largest animal known to be captured by a predaceous fungus is:
*Zoophagus* traps rotifers using:
c: 'Lethal lollipops'—sticky knobs the rotifers try to eat

questions.q: When the amoeba *Geococcus vulgaris* attacks *Dactylella passalopaga*, the fungus:
c: Gags it with a rapidly swelling bulbous outgrowth

questions.q: Why are amoeba-trapping hyphomycetes rare, according to Kendrick?
c: A fungus would need many tiny amoebae to gain enough energy to sporulate
